parts.label: ATEM Camera Control Panel chassis
parts.description: Desktop four-strip camera shading/control panel.

parts.label: IEC AC input
parts.description: Internal 100–240 V AC input

parts.label: 4-pin XLR DC input
parts.description: 12–30 V DC redundant input

parts.label: Ethernet 1
parts.description: 10/100/1000 BaseT network/control

parts.label: Ethernet loop
parts.description: Second GigE port for loop output

parts.label: USB-C service
parts.description: Firmware updates

parts.label: CH1 · LCD / soft controls
parts.description: Home screen for this CCU. It names the camera assigned to the strip and turns red when that camera is live. From here you reach the camera bank A/B switch, the recall-all toggle, the auxiliary output used for camera control, the master black enable, and the panel brightness.

parts.label: CH1 · Scene 1
parts.description: Recalls scene file 1 for this camera — every stored setting at once: shutter, master gain, white balance, colour balance and bars. To write the slot instead, press STORE first, then this button. If recall-all is enabled on the LCD home screen, pressing this recalls each CCU’s own scene 1 on every camera at once, including the camera currently on air, so the manual advises enabling recall-all only for a planned setup and turning it straight off again.

parts.label: CH1 · Scene 2
parts.description: Recalls scene file 2 for this camera — every stored setting at once: shutter, master gain, white balance, colour balance and bars. To write the slot instead, press STORE first, then this button. If recall-all is enabled on the LCD home screen, pressing this recalls each CCU’s own scene 2 on every camera at once, including the camera currently on air, so the manual advises enabling recall-all only for a planned setup and turning it straight off again.

parts.label: CH1 · Store scene
parts.description: Arms a scene-file save. Press STORE and it lights red to show the panel is waiting, then press one of the five numbered buttons to write every current setting for this camera into that slot.

parts.label: CH1 · ND filter
parts.description: Marked on the panel, but the cited manual states the ND setting "will be enabled in a future update". Whether current panel firmware implements it has not been verified here, so treat the control as unproven rather than assuming it drives the camera.

parts.label: CH1 · Color correction
parts.description: Marked on the panel, but the cited manual states the CC setting "will be enabled in a future update". Whether current panel firmware implements it has not been verified here.

parts.label: CH1 · Master gain
parts.description: Master gain for this camera, stepped by the up and down arrows. Raising it buys exposure in dim light at the cost of electronic noise, which becomes obvious at the top of the range. The down arrow lights when gain is negative and the up arrow lights when it is positive, so the lit arrow tells you which side of zero you are on at a glance.

parts.label: CH1 · Shutter
parts.description: Shutter speed for this camera. Slower shutter brightens the picture by exposing the sensor for longer, which is usually a better first move than adding gain because it adds no noise, and it is also how you kill flicker under mains-frequency lighting. Faster shutter cuts motion blur for sharp action, at the cost of light.

parts.label: CH1 · White balance
parts.description: White balance for this camera. Light sources are warm or cool, and this shifts colour temperature to compensate so that whites stay white rather than drifting orange under tungsten or blue under daylight.

parts.label: CH1 · Color bars
parts.description: Enables or disables colour bars on this camera’s output. Bars are a line-up reference; anything sending bars is not sending a picture, so check what is on air before pressing it.

parts.label: CH1 · Relative iris mode
parts.description: Relative and absolute describe how the panel resyncs when a setting is changed somewhere else, such as in ATEM Software Control. In relative mode the panel eases back into sync as you make your next adjustment, so the change is almost invisible. In absolute mode the value snaps to wherever the physical control is sitting the moment you touch it, which is abrupt and can be ugly on air. Decide which mode you are in before the show rather than during it. The cited manual describes the ON button as cycling between the two modes.

parts.label: CH1 · Absolute iris mode
parts.description: Relative and absolute describe how the panel resyncs when a setting is changed somewhere else, such as in ATEM Software Control. In relative mode the panel eases back into sync as you make your next adjustment, so the change is almost invisible. In absolute mode the value snaps to wherever the physical control is sitting the moment you touch it, which is abrupt and can be ugly on air. Decide which mode you are in before the show rather than during it. The cited manual describes the ON button as cycling between the two modes.

parts.label: CH1 · White R
parts.description: Red content of the gain, meaning the highlights. Despite sitting near the white balance controls this is not white balance — it trims the red channel at the bright end of the picture.

parts.label: CH1 · White G
parts.description: Green content of the gain, meaning the highlights. This trims the green channel at the bright end of the picture, separately from white balance.

parts.label: CH1 · White B
parts.description: Blue content of the gain, meaning the highlights. This trims the blue channel at the bright end of the picture, separately from white balance.

parts.label: CH1 · Black R
parts.description: Red content of the lift, meaning the shadows. Use it to remove a colour cast from the darkest part of the picture without disturbing the highlights.

parts.label: CH1 · Black G
parts.description: Green content of the lift, meaning the shadows. Use it to remove a colour cast from the darkest part of the picture without disturbing the highlights.

parts.label: CH1 · Black B
parts.description: Blue content of the lift, meaning the shadows. Use it to remove a colour cast from the darkest part of the picture without disturbing the highlights.

parts.label: CH1 · Black / flare
parts.description: Reaches the gamma, meaning the mid tones. Hold this button down and turn the black RGB knobs, and they trim the mid tones instead of the shadows — so the same three knobs cover two tonal regions depending on whether this button is held.

parts.label: CH1 · Custom / Y gain
parts.description: Currently assigned to Y gain, which raises or lowers overall luminance without moving the individual colour channels. The cited manual describes the knob as freely assignable in a future update, so its function may differ on current firmware.

parts.label: CH1 · Camera number
parts.description: The large camera number for this strip, readable across a gallery. It illuminates red when this camera is live on the program output — the fastest way to check you are not about to shade a camera that is on air.

parts.label: CH1 · Iris / master black joystick
parts.description: The main shading control. Lean it forward or back to open and close the iris, and turn the ring wheel beneath the knob to raise or lower master black, the pedestal. Pressing the joystick down switches this camera to the auxiliary output assigned to camera control, so you can look at it full screen before adjusting.

parts.label: CH1 · Preview
parts.description: Sends this camera to the auxiliary output assigned to camera control, so the shot you are shading is the one you are looking at. Which aux that is depends on the switcher and is set on the panel’s LCD.

parts.label: CH1 · Sensitivity
parts.description: Sets how much of the iris range the joystick’s full travel covers. Tighten it when you want fine control around one exposure, widen it when you need to move a long way quickly.

parts.label: CH1 · Coarse
parts.description: Caps how far the iris can open, so an over-exposed picture cannot reach air. Set it by opening the iris fully, then bringing coarse down until exposure is right — from then on the joystick cannot go past that ceiling.

parts.label: CH1 · Iris / MB active
parts.description: Locks the joystick’s iris and master black so neither can be nudged by accident during a show. Master black can also be disabled globally from the panel’s LCD settings.

parts.label: CH1 · Auto iris
parts.description: Runs an automatic exposure on a lens with electronic iris control. It is a starting point rather than a set-and-forget — it responds to whatever is in frame at the moment you press it.

parts.label: CH1 · Call
parts.description: Flashes the tally on this camera to get the operator’s attention, on cameras that support it. Useful for signalling before going live.

parts.label: CH1 · Panel active
parts.description: Locks this CCU’s controls so nothing can be changed by a knock or a sleeve. Worth using on any camera that is parked and correct.

parts.label: CH1 · Status indicators
parts.description: Indicator for this strip, showing network, error and active states rather than anything about the picture.

parts.description: Recalls scene file 2 for this camera — every stored setting at once: shutter, master gain, white balance, colour balance and bars. To write the slot instead, press STORE first, then this button. If recall-all is enabled on the LCD home screen, pressing this recalls each CCU’s own scene 2 on every camera at once, including the camera currently on air, so the manual advises enabling recall-all only for a planned setup and turning it straight off again.

parts.label: CH4 · Scene 3
parts.description: Recalls scene file 3 for this camera — every stored setting at once: shutter, master gain, white balance, colour balance and bars. To write the slot instead, press STORE first, then this button. If recall-all is enabled on the LCD home screen, pressing this recalls each CCU’s own scene 3 on every camera at once, including the camera currently on air, so the manual advises enabling recall-all only for a planned setup and turning it straight off again.

parts.label: CH4 · Scene 4
parts.description: Recalls scene file 4 for this camera — every stored setting at once: shutter, master gain, white balance, colour balance and bars. To write the slot instead, press STORE first, then this button. If recall-all is enabled on the LCD home screen, pressing this recalls each CCU’s own scene 4 on every camera at once, including the camera currently on air, so the manual advises enabling recall-all only for a planned setup and turning it straight off again.

parts.label: CH4 · Scene 5
parts.description: Recalls scene file 5 for this camera — every stored setting at once: shutter, master gain, white balance, colour balance and bars. To write the slot instead, press STORE first, then this button. If recall-all is enabled on the LCD home screen, pressing this recalls each CCU’s own scene 5 on every camera at once, including the camera currently on air, so the manual advises enabling recall-all only for a planned setup and turning it straight off again.

parts.label: CH4 · Store scene
parts.description: Arms a scene-file save. Press STORE and it lights red to show the panel is waiting, then press one of the five numbered buttons to write every current setting for this camera into that slot.

parts.label: CH4 · ND filter
parts.description: Marked on the panel, but the cited manual states the ND setting "will be enabled in a future update". Whether current panel firmware implements it has not been verified here, so treat the control as unproven rather than assuming it drives the camera.

parts.label: CH4 · Color correction
parts.description: Marked on the panel, but the cited manual states the CC setting "will be enabled in a future update". Whether current panel firmware implements it has not been verified here.

parts.label: CH4 · Master gain
parts.description: Master gain for this camera, stepped by the up and down arrows. Raising it buys exposure in dim light at the cost of electronic noise, which becomes obvious at the top of the range. The down arrow lights when gain is negative and the up arrow lights when it is positive, so the lit arrow tells you which side of zero you are on at a glance.

parts.label: CH4 · Shutter
parts.description: Shutter speed for this camera. Slower shutter brightens the picture by exposing the sensor for longer, which is usually a better first move than adding gain because it adds no noise, and it is also how you kill flicker under mains-frequency lighting. Faster shutter cuts motion blur for sharp action, at the cost of light.

parts.label: CH4 · White balance
parts.description: White balance for this camera. Light sources are warm or cool, and this shifts colour temperature to compensate so that whites stay white rather than drifting orange under tungsten or blue under daylight.

parts.label: CH4 · Color bars
parts.description: Enables or disables colour bars on this camera’s output. Bars are a line-up reference; anything sending bars is not sending a picture, so check what is on air before pressing it.

parts.label: CH4 · Relative iris mode
parts.description: Relative and absolute describe how the panel resyncs when a setting is changed somewhere else, such as in ATEM Software Control. In relative mode the panel eases back into sync as you make your next adjustment, so the change is almost invisible. In absolute mode the value snaps to wherever the physical control is sitting the moment you touch it, which is abrupt and can be ugly on air. Decide which mode you are in before the show rather than during it. The cited manual describes the ON button as cycling between the two modes.

parts.label: CH4 · Absolute iris mode
parts.description: Relative and absolute describe how the panel resyncs when a setting is changed somewhere else, such as in ATEM Software Control. In relative mode the panel eases back into sync as you make your next adjustment, so the change is almost invisible. In absolute mode the value snaps to wherever the physical control is sitting the moment you touch it, which is abrupt and can be ugly on air. Decide which mode you are in before the show rather than during it. The cited manual describes the ON button as cycling between the two modes.

parts.label: CH4 · White R
parts.description: Red content of the gain, meaning the highlights. Despite sitting near the white balance controls this is not white balance — it trims the red channel at the bright end of the picture.

parts.label: CH4 · White G
parts.description: Green content of the gain, meaning the highlights. This trims the green channel at the bright end of the picture, separately from white balance.

parts.label: CH4 · White B
parts.description: Blue content of the gain, meaning the highlights. This trims the blue channel at the bright end of the picture, separately from white balance.

parts.label: CH4 · Black R
parts.description: Red content of the lift, meaning the shadows. Use it to remove a colour cast from the darkest part of the picture without disturbing the highlights.

parts.label: CH4 · Black G
parts.description: Green content of the lift, meaning the shadows. Use it to remove a colour cast from the darkest part of the picture without disturbing the highlights.

parts.label: CH4 · Black B
parts.description: Blue content of the lift, meaning the shadows. Use it to remove a colour cast from the darkest part of the picture without disturbing the highlights.

parts.label: CH4 · Black / flare
parts.description: Reaches the gamma, meaning the mid tones. Hold this button down and turn the black RGB knobs, and they trim the mid tones instead of the shadows — so the same three knobs cover two tonal regions depending on whether this button is held.

parts.label: CH4 · Custom / Y gain
parts.description: Currently assigned to Y gain, which raises or lowers overall luminance without moving the individual colour channels. The cited manual describes the knob as freely assignable in a future update, so its function may differ on current firmware.

parts.label: CH4 · Camera number
parts.description: The large camera number for this strip, readable across a gallery. It illuminates red when this camera is live on the program output — the fastest way to check you are not about to shade a camera that is on air.

parts.label: CH4 · Iris / master black joystick
parts.description: The main shading control. Lean it forward or back to open and close the iris, and turn the ring wheel beneath the knob to raise or lower master black, the pedestal. Pressing the joystick down switches this camera to the auxiliary output assigned to camera control, so you can look at it full screen before adjusting.

parts.label: CH4 · Preview
parts.description: Sends this camera to the auxiliary output assigned to camera control, so the shot you are shading is the one you are looking at. Which aux that is depends on the switcher and is set on the panel’s LCD.

parts.label: CH4 · Sensitivity
parts.description: Sets how much of the iris range the joystick’s full travel covers. Tighten it when you want fine control around one exposure, widen it when you need to move a long way quickly.

parts.label: CH4 · Coarse
parts.description: Caps how far the iris can open, so an over-exposed picture cannot reach air. Set it by opening the iris fully, then bringing coarse down until exposure is right — from then on the joystick cannot go past that ceiling.

parts.label: CH4 · Iris / MB active
parts.description: Locks the joystick’s iris and master black so neither can be nudged by accident during a show. Master black can also be disabled globally from the panel’s LCD settings.

parts.label: CH4 · Auto iris
parts.description: Runs an automatic exposure on a lens with electronic iris control. It is a starting point rather than a set-and-forget — it responds to whatever is in frame at the moment you press it.

parts.label: CH4 · Call
parts.description: Flashes the tally on this camera to get the operator’s attention, on cameras that support it. Useful for signalling before going live.

parts.label: CH4 · Panel active
parts.description: Locks this CCU’s controls so nothing can be changed by a knock or a sleeve. Worth using on any camera that is parked and correct.

parts.label: CH4 · Status indicators
parts.description: Indicator for this strip, showing network, error and active states rather than anything about the picture.
